newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds slip in slow, listless market.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds slip in slow, listless market.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished lower Tuesday after a listless session with prices pulled down by U.S. Treasuries.
"It was not a very positive day," said an analyst at a foreign bank. Slim volumes and a lack of market-moving news kept the market from making any real headway during the session.
Argentina's FRB due 2005 was 1/8 lower at 91-3/8, while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was $0.05 down to 126.50.
A moribund U.S. Treasury market added to the lack of inspiration.

A lower-than-expected cut-off yield of 6.92 percent at the government's auction of $500 million in two-year Bonte Treasury bonds helped pull prices up from the day's lows but they still failed to end in positive territory.
Traders said the market would turn its attention to the release of U.S. consumer price figures on Wednesday.
In the money markets, call money rates were flat at 6.53 percent.
